notes: v2.5.3 — 2026-09-16 (the sequencer keeps its place, and the mixer stops lying) THE TRACK HEADERS TOOK YOUR CLICK 22 PIXELS AWAY. The arranger's hit tests spell the header origin TITLEH + CONTROLSH + OVERVIEWH + RULERH; paint spelled it TITLEH + CONTROLSH and added RULERH at each use. When the overview strip was inserted, paint never got it - so every control in the track headers was DRAWN in one place and CLICKED in another. Two spellings of one number is how that happens, and it shipped that way in 2.5.0, 2.5.1 and 2.5.2. A STRETCHED DRUM LOOP CLICKED ON EVERY WRAP. The WSOLA first grain skipped its rising window so the attack would survive - correct intent, but it meant sample 0 jumped straight to whatever the source held there. A source that does not start on a zero crossing therefore began with a STEP, and on a loop that step is a click every time round. Now a ~1 ms ramp: far too brief to soften a transient, long enough that there is no discontinuity left to hear. MPC MODE AND THE PATTERN SLOTS WERE BOTH WRITING THE SAME SAMPLES. Switching pattern while MPC was on saved the loop's CHOPS into the slot you were leaving
